title: Comment on “Surgical management of mandibular osteoradionecrosis: risk factors, timeline and surgical outcomes”
html: We read with interest the article by Kagan et al. on surgical outcomes of mandibular osteoradionecrosis (ORN) over seven years at a high-volume tertiary centre1. The authors are to be commended for providing detailed longitudinal data on a condition associated with substantial morbidity and potential mortality if not treated in a timely manner. Their description of surgical trajectories and postoperative symptom evolution is clinically valuable. However, we wish to highlight three related methodological considerations that are central to the interpretation of the reported dose–risk associations and comparative surgical outcomes in the current intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT)/volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) era.
